What are some long-living plants or trees that can thrive in hot, dry climates, and how can I care for them to ensure they stay healthy and productive?

Which of these four candidate replies is the best, most personalized response for me? Answer with the single letter (A, B, C, or D) of the best option.

Water deeply on a spaced schedule to push roots down, and ensure good drainage to guard against excess moisture. Light seasonal pruning will keep them healthy and fruiting well.

(B) In a hot, arid climate, long-living options include olive trees, pomegranates, and hardy citrus varieties. Provide deep, occasional watering to promote strong roots, ensure the soil drains well, and prune lightly each season to keep them vigorous and productive.

(C) In a hot, arid climate, the date palm will serve you well for decades, as will drought-tolerant olive trees and fragrant rosemary. Deep, occasional watering and loose, well-draining soil will help these thrive, and maintaining them can be a relaxing way to spend quiet weekends without extended family gatherings.

(D) In a hot, arid climate, date palms are a classic long-living choice, along with figs and pomegranates. For best results, give your palms deep but infrequent watering to encourage strong root systems, and keep the soil well-drained to prevent rot. Occasional pruning of older fronds will maintain airflow and vigor, ensuring steady productivity.
gold_answer: B — In a hot, arid climate, long-living options include olive trees, pomegranates, and hardy citrus varieties. Provide deep, occasional watering to promote strong roots, ensure the soil drains well, and prune lightly each season to keep them vigorous and productive.

(D) When friends become less present in your life, it’s natural to feel the ache of their absence.
